lessons.title: Time Value of Money
lessons.html:
The Time Value of Money (TVM) is the single most fundamental concept in all of finance. Every calculation in this unit — present value, future value, valuation of assets, opportunity cost — is built on this one idea: a sum of money available today is worth more than the identical sum available in the future.

This is not an opinion or a cultural convention. It is a mathematical and economic reality that applies universally — in Tashkent, Tokyo, or New York. Once you truly understand the time value of money, you will never look at financial decisions the same way again.

The Three Reasons Money Has a Time Value

There are exactly three reasons why money today is worth more than money tomorrow. All three are real and all three operate simultaneously in every financial market.

  • Reason 1: Investment Opportunity: Money you hold today can be put to work immediately. You can

deposit it in a bank, buy assets, start a business, or invest in stocks. Each of these generates a return. A sum that sits idle in the future produces nothing today. This is the most important reason — money has productive potential, and time is required to realize it.

  • Reason 2: Inflation: In virtually every economy, prices rise over time. In Uzbekistan, inflation

averaged 8–12% annually in recent years. This means 1,000,000 UZS today buys more goods and services than 1,000,000 UZS will in five years. The purchasing power of money erodes continuously. Holding uninvested cash is therefore not neutral — it is a guaranteed loss in real terms.

  • Reason 3: Risk and Uncertainty: The future is uncertain. A promise of money in the future carries

the risk that it may never arrive: the borrower may default, the investment may fail, political or economic events may intervene. Money held today is certain. Money promised in the future is not. Rational people require compensation for this uncertainty — which is why future money is discounted.

The Core Principle of TVM

Given a choice between receiving 1,000,000 UZS today or 1,000,000 UZS one year from now, a rational person always chooses today. Not out of impatience or greed — but because today's money can be invested to earn returns, its purchasing power is higher, and it carries no collection risk. This preference for present money over future money is called the time preference for money, and it is the foundation of everything in this unit.

A Concrete Illustration

Let's make this very concrete. Suppose you lend a friend 2,000,000 UZS today. He promises to return it in 3 years. What is the "fair" repayment?

If he returns exactly 2,000,000 UZS, you have actually lost money. Here is why:

  • You gave up the ability to invest that money for 3 years. At a conservative 12% per year bank deposit,

2,000,000 UZS would have grown to 2,000,000 × (1.12)3 = 2,809,856 UZS.

  • Inflation at 8% per year means 2,000,000 UZS in 3 years buys what approximately 1,587,600 UZS

buys today.

  • You took on the risk that your friend might not pay at all.

The fair repayment is approximately 2,809,856 UZS — not 2,000,000. The extra 809,856 UZS is the compensation for time, inflation, and risk. This is exactly what interest is — not an arbitrary fee, but the mathematically correct price of borrowing money across time.

— WORKED EXAMPLE — WORKED EXAMPLE — TVM in a Real Uzbekistan Context

Scenario: You have 10,000,000 UZS in cash under your mattress for 2 years.

Bank deposit rate: 14% per year. Inflation: 9% per year.

After 2 years, your cash is still 10,000,000 UZS nominally.

BUT: If you had deposited it, you would have: 10,000,000 × (1.14)² = 12,996,000 UZS.

AND: Due to inflation, your 10,000,000 UZS only buys what 8,416,800 UZS bought 2 years ago.

Net result of holding cash: You "lost" approximately 4,579,200 UZS in opportunity terms.

Lesson: There is no such thing as "safe" cash under a mattress. Inaction is a decision with a cost.

Why This Matters for Every Financial Decision

Once you understand TVM, you realize that every financial decision involves comparing money at different points in time. This is true whether you are:

  • Deciding whether to buy a car now or save for it

  • Evaluating whether a business investment is worthwhile

  • Choosing between two job offers with different pay structures

  • Deciding when to buy a house

  • Comparing investment options with different time horizons

In every case, to compare fairly, you must convert all cash flows to the same point in time. That is what Present Value and Future Value calculations allow us to do.

lessons.title: Present Value (PV)
lessons.html:
Present Value (PV) is the current value of a future sum of money, given a specific rate of return (the discount rate). In other words, it answers the question: "How much is a payment I will receive in the future worth to me right now?"

PV is one of the most powerful tools in all of finance because it allows us to compare money received at completely different points in time on a fair, equal basis. Without PV, we cannot evaluate investments, value businesses, price bonds, or make rational borrowing decisions.

The Present Value Formula

The formula for calculating Present Value is:

Step-by-Step: How to Calculate PV

Let's work through a complete calculation step by step, so you can apply it to any situation.

— WORKED EXAMPLE — WORKED EXAMPLE — Full PV Calculation

Problem: You will receive 15,000,000 UZS in 4 years. You can earn 10% per year on alternative investments. What is 15,000,000 UZS worth to you TODAY?

Step 1: Identify the inputs.

FV = 15,000,000 r = 0.10 n = 4

Step 2: Calculate the discount factor.

(1 + r)^n = (1.10)^4 = 1.10 × 1.10 × 1.10 × 1.10 = 1.4641

Step 3: Divide FV by the discount factor.

PV = 15,000,000 ÷ 1.4641 = 10,245,181 UZS

Interpretation: Receiving 15,000,000 UZS in 4 years is equivalent to receiving 10,245,181 UZS today, assuming you can earn 10% per year. If someone wants to sell you a right to receive 15M in 4 years, you should pay NO MORE than 10,245,181 UZS for it.

How the Discount Rate Affects PV

The discount rate is the most powerful variable in the PV formula. Even small changes in the rate produce large differences in present value, especially over long time horizons. The higher the rate, the less future money is worth today.

What Is the Right Discount Rate to Use?

Choosing the correct discount rate is one of the most important and debated questions in finance. The discount rate should represent the opportunity cost of capital — the return you could earn on an alternative investment of similar risk.

  • For a very safe investment: use a low rate (e.g., 10–14% in Uzbekistan, matching bank deposits)

  • For a medium-risk investment (real estate, established business): use 15–20%

  • For a high-risk investment (startup, crypto): use 25–40% or higher

  • For valuing corporate projects: use the company's cost of capital (covered in Unit 3)

Key Insight on Discount Rates

If you use too LOW a discount rate, you will overvalue investments and overpay. If you use too HIGH a rate, you will undervalue them and miss opportunities. The art of finance is choosing the right rate that accurately reflects the risk of the cash flows being valued. This is why financial analysts spend enormous effort debating and calculating discount rates.

lessons.title: Future Value (FV)
lessons.html:
Future Value (FV) is the mirror image of Present Value. Where PV asks "what is future money worth today?", FV asks "what will today's money be worth in the future?" Future value is the mathematical engine behind compound interest — and understanding it is the key to building wealth over time.

The Future Value Formula

FV = PV × (1 + r)n

— WORKED EXAMPLE — WORKED EXAMPLE — Full FV Calculation

Problem: You invest 5,000,000 UZS today at 12% per year. How much will you have in 5 years?

Step 1: Identify inputs.

PV = 5,000,000 r = 0.12 n = 5

Step 2: Calculate (1 + r)^n.

(1.12)^5 = 1.12 × 1.12 × 1.12 × 1.12 × 1.12 = 1.7623

Step 3: Multiply PV by the growth factor.

FV = 5,000,000 × 1.7623 = 8,811,709 UZS

Your 5,000,000 UZS grows to 8,811,709 UZS in 5 years. The extra 3,811,709 UZS is the return on your investment — interest on interest.

Simple Interest vs. Compound Interest

Before going further, it is critical to understand the difference between simple and compound interest. They produce dramatically different outcomes, especially over long periods — and this difference is at the heart of why starting to invest early matters so much.

Simple Interest

With simple interest, you earn interest ONLY on the original amount (principal). No matter how long you invest, the interest earned each period is the same fixed amount.

FV (Simple) = PV × (1 + r × n)

Example: 1,000,000 UZS at 10% simple interest for 5 years.

  • Year 1: 1,000,000 + 100,000 = 1,100,000 UZS

  • Year 2: 1,100,000 + 100,000 = 1,200,000 UZS

  • Year 5: 1,000,000 × (1 + 0.10 × 5) = 1,500,000 UZS

Growth is LINEAR — the same 100,000 UZS every year.

Compound Interest

With compound interest, you earn interest on your principal AND on all previously earned interest. Your interest earns interest. This creates exponential (accelerating) growth.

FV (Compound) = PV × (1 + r)n

Example: 1,000,000 UZS at 10% compound interest for 5 years.

  • Year 1: 1,000,000 × 1.10 = 1,100,000 UZS (interest: 100,000)

  • Year 2: 1,100,000 × 1.10 = 1,210,000 UZS (interest: 110,000)

  • Year 3: 1,210,000 × 1.10 = 1,331,000 UZS (interest: 121,000)

  • Year 5: 1,000,000 × (1.10) = 1,610,510 UZS

Growth is EXPONENTIAL — the interest earned each year is LARGER than the year before, because it compounds on a larger and larger base.

The lesson: Time in the market is more powerful than the amount you invest. Start now.

lessons.title: Opportunity Cost of Capital
lessons.html:
The Opportunity Cost of Capital is the return you give up by choosing one investment over the next best available alternative of similar risk. It is arguably the most important — and most overlooked — concept in personal finance.

Every financial decision has an opportunity cost. When you put money into one investment, you automatically forgo every other thing you could have done with that money. The opportunity cost is not the worst thing you gave up — it is the BEST thing you gave up.

Understanding Opportunity Cost: A Simple Example

You have 5,000,000 UZS. You are considering three options:

  • Option A: Bank deposit at 14% per year (safe, guaranteed)

  • Option B: Real estate investment, expected return 20% per year

  • Option C: Start a small business, expected return 30% per year (but risky)

If you choose Option B (real estate), your opportunity cost is 14% — the safe guaranteed return you gave up from Option A. To justify choosing real estate over the bank, you must believe the extra risk of real estate is worth the extra 6% expected return (20% − 14%).

If you choose Option C (business), your opportunity cost is still 14% (the next best safe alternative). But now you are taking on significant additional risk for 30% − 14% = 16% extra return. Is 16% enough compensation for the risk of losing everything? That is a judgment call — but opportunity cost gives you the framework to make it rationally.

The Opportunity Cost IS the Discount Rate

There is a direct connection between opportunity cost and Present Value. The discount rate you use in PV calculations IS the opportunity cost of capital. This is not a coincidence — it is the definition.

When you ask "what is a future cash flow worth today?", you are really asking: "How much would I need to invest today — at my opportunity cost rate — to replicate that future payment?" The present value IS the amount you'd invest today in your best alternative to produce the same future result.

The Hidden Costs of Everyday Decisions

Opportunity cost thinking transforms how you evaluate ordinary decisions. It reveals that "free" choices often have significant hidden costs.

  • Leaving cash in a low-interest account: If your bank pays 5% but you could earn 14% in a deposit

account, you are losing 9% per year on every sum you leave there. On 10,000,000 UZS, that is 900,000 UZS per year in foregone returns.

  • Keeping money at home: Cash under a mattress earns 0%. With 12% inflation, you are losing 12%

of purchasing power per year. This is not "safe" — it is a certain loss.

  • Buying an expensive item instead of investing: A 5,000,000 UZS luxury purchase is not just a 5M

cost. At 15% per year for 20 years, that money would have grown to 81,833,000 UZS. The true cost of the purchase is 81 million — the future value of what you gave up.

The Most Important Insight

The opportunity cost framework means there is NO SUCH THING as a "neutral" financial decision. Every choice you make with money — including choosing to do nothing — has a cost. The financially literate person always asks: "What am I giving up by making this choice?" and only proceeds if the benefits exceed the full opportunity cost.

lessons.title: Valuation of Assets
lessons.html:
Valuation is the process of determining what an asset is actually worth today. It is one of the most important skills in all of finance — whether you are buying a stock, a property, a business, or a bond, you need to know: is the price being asked fair, too high, or too low?

The universal principle of valuation: Any asset is worth the present value of all the future cash flows it will generate for its owner. This single sentence contains the entire theory of valuation. Everything else is detail.

Value of Any Asset = PV of All Future Cash Flows

Net Present Value (NPV)

Net Present Value is the most important valuation tool in finance. NPV answers the question: "If I invest money today and receive cash flows in the future, am I better off than if I had invested at my opportunity cost rate?"

NPV is calculated by taking the present value of all future cash flows from an investment and subtracting the initial cost:

NPV = ∑ [CFt ÷ (1 + r)t] − Initial Investment

Where CF is the cash flow in period t, r is the discount rate (opportunity cost of capital), and t runs from period 1 to the end of the investment.

Total PV = 6,956,522 + 7,561,437 + 7,890,257 + 6,861,963 + 27,344,481 = 56,614,660 UZS

NPV = 56,614,660 − 50,000,000 = +6,614,660 UZS

Decision: NPV is POSITIVE — this investment creates 6.6M UZS of value above the opportunity cost. ACCEPT.

Valuing Stocks

A share of stock represents ownership in a company. Its value equals the present value of all future dividends plus the eventual sale price. In practice, analysts use several approaches:

  • Dividend Discount Model: Value = Dividend ÷ (Discount Rate − Dividend Growth Rate). Used for

stable dividend-paying companies. Example: A company pays 5,000 UZS dividend per share, expected to grow 4% per year. If your discount rate is 14%, value = 5,000 ÷ (0.14 − 0.04) = 50,000 UZS per share.

  • Price-to-Earnings (P/E) Ratio: Stock Price ÷ Earnings Per Share. A quick comparison tool. If the

market average P/E is 15 and a company earns 10,000 UZS per share, a "fair" price is approximately 150,000 UZS. A stock trading below this is potentially undervalued.

  • Discounted Cash Flow (DCF): Projects the company's free cash flows for 5–10 years, then

discounts them back to the present. The most rigorous method, used by professional analysts.

Valuing Bonds

A bond is a loan you make to a company or government. In return, they promise to pay you fixed interest (coupon) payments at regular intervals, plus repay the principal at maturity. The value of a bond is simply the PV of all these future cash flows.

  • Coupon payments: Fixed interest paid periodically (e.g., 8% of face value per year).

  • Face value (principal): Repaid at the end of the bond's life (e.g., 1,000,000 UZS in 5 years).

  • Critical rule: When market interest rates RISE, existing bond prices FALL — because the fixed future

payments are now discounted at a higher rate, reducing their PV. When rates FALL, bond prices RISE.

Valuing Real Estate

Real estate generates value through rental income and property appreciation. The two main valuation approaches are:

  • Income Approach: Value = Annual Net Rental Income ÷ Capitalization Rate. The "cap rate" is similar

to a discount rate for property. Example: An apartment generates 24,000,000 UZS net per year. If the cap rate is 8%, value = 24,000,000 ÷ 0.08 = 300,000,000 UZS.

  • Comparable Sales Approach: Value based on recent prices of similar properties in the same area.

Most commonly used in residential real estate.

— WORKED EXAMPLE — WORKED EXAMPLE — Real Estate Valuation

Apartment in Tashkent: purchase price 200,000,000 UZS.

Annual rental income: 20,000,000 UZS. Annual expenses: 2,000,000 UZS.

Net income: 18,000,000 UZS per year.

Expected sale price after 10 years: 350,000,000 UZS.

Your required return: 12% per year.

PV of rental income (10 years at 12%):

Using annuity formula: 18,000,000 × [(1 − (1.12)^{-10}) ÷ 0.12] = 18,000,000 × 5.650 = 101,700,000 UZS

PV of sale price: 350,000,000 ÷ (1.12)^{10} = 350,000,000 ÷ 3.1058 = 112,700,000 UZS

Total Value = 101,700,000 + 112,700,000 = 214,400,000 UZS

NPV = 214,400,000 − 200,000,000 = +14,400,000 UZS

Decision: The apartment is worth MORE than it costs — a positive NPV investment. Buy it.

lessons.title: Risk & Return
lessons.html:
Risk and return are the two most fundamental concepts in investment decision-making, and they are inseparable. In finance, higher expected return always comes with higher risk. Always. Without exception. Anyone promising high returns with no risk is either misinformed or deliberately misleading you.

Understanding the risk-return relationship is not just academic. It is the framework that protects your savings from fraud, helps you build a rational investment portfolio, and allows you to make financial decisions without being paralyzed by fear or seduced by greed.

What Is Risk in Finance?

In everyday language, "risk" means the chance that something bad happens. In finance, risk has a more precise meaning: risk is the uncertainty or variability of future returns. An investment is "risky" not because it will definitely lose money, but because its future value is uncertain — it could be much higher or much lower than expected.

Why Higher Return Demands Higher Risk

If a high-return investment were also completely safe, everyone would put all their money there. The flood of demand would drive up the price until the return fell to a level that reflected the risk. Markets are competitive: any genuine free lunch gets arbitraged away immediately. High returns exist only because investors demand extra compensation for bearing extra uncertainty.

This is why a 30% return from a startup sounds attractive — until you remember that most startups fail completely. The high expected return is compensation for the very real probability of losing everything.

Diversification: The One Free Lunch

While the risk-return tradeoff cannot be eliminated entirely, it can be managed through diversification — spreading investments across multiple assets that do not move together perfectly.

When one investment falls, another may rise or hold steady. The overall portfolio becomes more stable than any individual holding, without necessarily sacrificing expected return. This is why diversification is called "the only free lunch in finance."

  • Within asset classes: Do not put all money in one stock — own 15–20+ across different industries

  • Across asset classes: Mix deposits, bonds, real estate, and stocks

  • Across geographies: Invest in Uzbekistan AND international markets (USD assets protect against

UZS devaluation)

  • Across time: Invest regularly (monthly) rather than all at once — reduces timing risk

— WORKED EXAMPLE — WORKED EXAMPLE — The Cost of Concentration

Scenario A — Concentrated: You invest all 20,000,000 UZS in one company stock.

The company goes bankrupt. You lose everything. Portfolio value: 0.

Scenario B — Diversified: You invest 1,000,000 UZS each in 20 different companies.

Three companies go bankrupt (a very bad year). You lose 3,000,000.

Portfolio value: 17,000,000 UZS — you are still in the game.

Both portfolios started identically. The only difference was concentration vs. diversification. Diversification did not prevent losses — but it prevented catastrophic, unrecoverable loss.

This is the purpose of diversification: not to maximize returns, but to survive bad outcomes.

Building a Simple Investment Pyramid

For a beginner investor in Uzbekistan, a simple pyramid approach helps structure your portfolio by risk level:

  • Foundation (50–60%): Safe, liquid assets — bank deposits, government bonds. These are your

emergency fund and low-risk base. Never put this at risk.

  • Middle layer (25–30%): Medium-risk investments — real estate, established businesses, index

funds. Long-term growth with manageable volatility.

  • Top layer (10–20%): Higher-risk investments — individual stocks, startup investments. Only money

you can afford to lose entirely. High potential upside.

Key Takeaway for 2.6

Never invest money you cannot afford to lose in high-risk assets. Never chase high returns without understanding what risk you are taking on. The goal of investing is not to maximize return — it is to maximize return FOR A GIVEN LEVEL OF RISK YOU CAN COMFORTABLY BEAR. Build your foundation first. Grow from there. Be patient. Compound interest and diversification are your most powerful tools.

glossary.title: Key Terms Glossary
glossary.html:
All Important Definitions from Unit 2

Time Value of Money

The principle that money available today is worth more than the same amount in the future, because today's money can be invested to earn returns, purchasing power is higher today, and the future is uncertain.

Present Value (PV)

The current worth of a future sum of money, discounted at an appropriate rate. Answers: "What is this future payment worth to me today?" Formula: PV = FV ÷ (1 + r)^n.

Future Value (FV)

The value that a sum of money invested today will grow to at a specified future date, given a certain rate of return. Formula: FV = PV × (1 + r)^n.

Discount Rate

The interest rate used to convert future cash flows into their present value. Represents the opportunity cost of capital — the return you could earn on an alternative investment of similar risk.

Compound Interest

Interest calculated on both the original principal AND all previously accumulated interest. Produces exponential growth over time. The most powerful force in personal wealth building.

Simple Interest

Interest calculated only on the original principal, not on accumulated interest. Produces linear (straight-line) growth. Less powerful than compound interest over time.

Opportunity Cost of

Capital

The return you give up by choosing one investment over the next best alternative of similar risk. This IS the discount rate used in present value calculations.

Net Present Value

(NPV)

The sum of the present values of all future cash flows from an investment, minus the initial cost. NPV > 0 means the investment creates value; NPV < 0 means it destroys value.

Valuation

The process of determining the current fair value of an asset or company. Based on the universal principle that any asset is worth the present value of all the cash flows it will generate.

Intrinsic Value

The true economic value of an asset based on fundamental analysis — the present value of all expected future cash flows. May differ significantly from market price.

Discount Factor

The multiplier (1 + r)^n used to convert a future cash flow to present value. Always less than 1 (for positive r), reflecting that future money is worth less today.

Annuity

A series of equal cash flows paid or received at regular intervals over a specified period. Common examples: mortgage payments, bond coupons, rental income.

Diversification

The strategy of spreading investments across multiple assets, industries, and geographies to reduce risk without necessarily reducing expected return. The "only free lunch" in finance.

Risk-Return Tradeoff

The fundamental principle that higher potential returns always come with higher risk. Investors require higher expected returns to compensate for bearing greater uncertainty.

Capitalization Rate

(Cap Rate)

Used in real estate: Cap Rate = Net Annual Income ÷ Property Value. Used to quickly

value

and

compare

investment

opportunities.

Rule of 72

A mental shortcut: Years to double your money ≈ 72 ÷ Annual Interest Rate (%). Quick way to estimate the effect of compound growth without a calculator.

lessons.title: Временная стоимость денег
lessons.html:
Временная стоимость денег (англ. Time Value of Money, TVM) — это фундаментальный принцип всей финансовой науки. Каждое финансовое решение — сберечь, инвестировать, взять кредит или потратить — основано на этом принципе.

Главная идея

Деньги, доступные СЕГОДНЯ, стоят больше, чем та же сумма в БУДУЩЕМ.

Это не только очевидно. Глубже вопрос: ПОЧЕМУ? И на КОЛЬКО больше? Понимание причин — это то, что отделяет финансовую грамотность от незнания.

Три причины, почему сегодняшние деньги ценнее

Причина 1: Инвестиционная возможность

Деньги, которые есть у вас сегодня, можно немедленно пустить в работу: положить в банк, вложить в бизнес, купить активы, которые растут в цене. 1 000 000 сум сегодня под 14% годовых через год станут 1 140 000 сум. Обещанный 1 000 000 сум через год эту возможность уже упустил.

Причина 2: Инфляция

Инфляция постепенно снижает покупательную способность денег. 1 000 000 сум сегодня купит больше товаров и услуг, чем через 5 лет. В Узбекистане инфляция в 2024 году составила около 8,5%. Деньги, просто лежащие без дела, каждый год теряют в реальной стоимости.

Причина 3: Риск и неопределённость

Будущее неопределённо. Любое обещание денег в будущем несёт риск: человек может не заплатить, бизнес может обанкротиться. Деньги в руках — без риска неполучения. Поэтому рациональные люди требуют компенсацию за ожидание.

Главный вывод

Имея выбор между получением любой суммы сегодня или той же суммы в будущем, рациональный человек всегда выберет деньги сегодня. Чтобы будущая выплата была эквивалентна текущей, она должна быть БОЛЬШЕ — чтобы компенсировать все три фактора. Именно поэтому проценты существуют.

Вариант A: Банковский депозит под 14% — доход 2 800 000 сум/год (почти без риска)

lessons.title: Pulning vaqt qiymati
lessons.html:
Pulning vaqt qiymati - bu butun moliya fanining asosi. Har qanday moliyaviy qaror - qarz olish, investitsiya qilish, tejash - aynan shu bir tamoyilga tayanadi: bugungi pul kelajakdagi bir xil miqdordagi puldan qimmatroq.

Bu gapni eshitganda odatda 'unda nimasi bor' deyishadi. Lekin asosiy savol - NIMA UCHUN va QANCHA qimmatroq? Mana shu savolga javob bera olish - moliyaviy savodxonlikning belgisi.

Asosiy g'oya

Tasavvur qiling: sizga ikki tanlov berildi - 1 000 000 so'mni HOZIR olasizmi yoki bir yildan keyin? Aqlli inson har doim HOZIR tanlaydi. Lekin nega?

3 ta asosiy sabab

1-sabab: Investitsiya imkoniyati

Bugun qo'lingizda pul bo'lsa, uni darhol ishga solishingiz mumkin. Bankka qo'ysangiz - foiz olasiz. Biznesga solsangiz - daromad keladi. 1 000 000 so'mni yillik 14% bilan bankka qo'ysangiz, bir yildan keyin 1 140 000 bo'ladi.

Bir yildan keyin va'da qilingan 1 000 000 so'm - bu imkoniyatni yo'qotgan degani. Siz o'sha 140 000 so'm foizdan mahrum bo'ldingiz.

2-sabab: Inflyatsiya

Inflyatsiya - narxlarning asta-sekin ko'tarilishi. Bugun 1 000 000 so'mga ko'proq narsa sotib olasiz, kelajakda esa o'sha pul bilan kamroq. O'zbekistonda 2024 yilda inflyatsiya ~8,5% edi.

Ya'ni, hech narsa qilmasangiz ham, 1 yil o'tgach, o'sha 1 000 000 so'mingizning real qiymati taxminan 915 000 so'mga tushadi. Ko'rinmas yo'qotish - mana shu inflyatsiya.

3-sabab: Noaniqlik va xavf

Kelajak noaniq. Va'da qilingan pul kelmasligi mumkin: odam bankrot bo'lishi, kompaniya yopilishi yoki boshqa sabab bo'lishi mumkin. Qo'lingizdagi pul - hech qanday xavf yo'q. Kelajakdagi pul - har doim ma'lum darajada xavf bor.

lessons.title: Kelajak qiymati (FV)
lessons.html:
Kelajak qiymati (Future Value, FV) - joriy qiymatning teskari hisobidir. U savolga javob beradi: Bugun investitsiya qilingan pul kelajakda qancha bo'ladi?

Moliyaviy rejalashtirish uchun zarur: 'Har yili 2 000 000 so'm tejasam, 20 yildan keyin qancha to'playman?' 'Bugun 10 000 000 so'mni 15% stavkada investitsiya qilsam, 10 yildan keyin qancha bo'ladi?' - bularning hammasi FV hisobi.

Kelajak qiymati formulasi

FV = PV x (1 + r)^n

Bu formula PV formulasini qayta tartiblagandan keyin hosil bo'ladi. PV va FV bir-biri bilan (1+r)^n koeffitsienti orqali bog'langan.

Oddiy foiz va murakkab foiz - farq nima?

Bu moliyaviy savodxonlikning eng muhim farqlaridan biri. Ikkalasi ham bir xil stavkada ishlaydi - lekin vaqt o'tishi bilan natija juda katta farq qiladi.

Oddiy foiz

Faqat boshlang'ich summa ustidan foiz hisoblanadi. Oldingi yillarda to'plangan foiz yangi foiz topmaydi. O'sish to'g'ri chiziqli.

Misol: 1 000 000 so'm, 10% oddiy foiz, 5 yil:

  • Har yili: 1 000 000 x 10% = 100 000 so'm foiz

  • 5 yildan keyin: 1 000 000 + (100 000 x 5) = 1 500 000 so'm

Murakkab foiz

Boshlang'ich summa VA oldingi foizlar ustidan ham foiz hisoblanadi. Har yili bazaviy summa ko'payadi - shuning uchun bir xil foiz stavkasida ko'proq pul ishlaydi.

Misol: 1 000 000 so'm, 10% murakkab foiz, 5 yil:

  • 1-yil: 1 000 000 x 1.10 = 1 100 000 (100 000 foiz)

  • 2-yil: 1 100 000 x 1.10 = 1 210 000 (110 000 foiz - ko'proq!)

  • 3-yil: 1 210 000 x 1.10 = 1 331 000 (121 000 foiz)

  • 4-yil: 1 331 000 x 1.10 = 1 464 100 (133 100 foiz)

  • 5-yil: 1 464 100 x 1.10 = 1 610 510 (146 410 foiz)

Jami: 1 610 510 so'm - oddiy foiz bilan 1 500 000 dan 110 510 so'm ko'p. Bu farq yillar o'tishi bilan katta tezda o'sadi.

lessons.title: Kapital alternativ xarajatlari
lessons.html:
Kapital alternativ xarajatlari (opportunity cost of capital) - moliyaning eng muhim va eng ko'p unutiladigan tushunchalaridan biri. U savolga javob beradi: Bir investitsiyani tanlash orqali qancha daromaddan voz kechdim?

Har safar pulni bir yo'lga sarflaganda, boshqa barcha imkoniyatlardan voz kechiladi. Alternativ xarajat - eng yaxshi o'tkazib yuborilgan imkoniyatning qiymati.

- AMALIY MISOL - Alternativ xarajatni aniqlash

Sizda 20 000 000 so'm bor. Uch tanlov:

A variant: Bankda 14% yillik - 2 800 000 so'm/yil (deyarli xavfsiz)

B variant: Biznesga investitsiya, kutilgan 22% - 4 400 000 so'm/yil (o'rtacha xavf)

C variant: Bitcoin, kutilgan 40% (juda yuqori xavf)

Agar B ni tanlasangiz:

  • Alternativ xarajat = 14% (A - eng yaxshi xavfsiz muqobil)

  • B dan haqiqiy qo'shimcha foyda = 22% - 14% = 8% = 1 600 000 so'm/yil

  • Savol: bu 1 600 000 qo'shimcha pul biznes xavfini oqlayaptimi?

Agar C ni tanlasangiz:

  • Siz 14% xavfsiz daromaddan va 22% biznes daromadidan voz kechdingiz

  • Bitcoin dan taxminiy 40% - bu ikki muqobilni oqlashi kerak, USTIGA xavfni ham

Diskont stavkasi = Alternativ xarajat

PV hisoblashda ishlatiladigan 'diskont stavkasi' aslida alternativ xarajat hisoblanadi. Bu tasodifiy raqam emas - o'xshash xavfdagi eng yaxshi muqobil investitsiyadan kutilgan daromad.

lessons.title: Aktivlarni baholash
lessons.html:
Baholash - aktivning haqiqiy qiymatini aniqlash jarayoni. Bu aksiyalarga, obligatsiyalarga, ko'chmas mulkka, biznesga yoki pul oqimi hosil qiladigan har qanday narsaga tegishli.

Universal tamoyil: Aktiv keltiradigan barcha kelajakdagi pul oqimlarining joriy qiymatiga teng. Baholamdagi boshqa hamma narsa - shu tamoyilni PV formulasi bilan qo'llash.

Toshkentda kichik kafe ochish uchun 30 000 000 so'm sarflaysizmi?

Kutilgan pul oqimlari (barcha xarajatlardan keyin sof foyda):

1-yil: 6 000 000 so'm

5-yil: 10 000 000 so'm + 15 000 000 so'm (kafeni sotish)

Diskont stavkasi (alternativ xarajat): 12% yillik

Har bir pul oqimining PV si:

1-yil: 6 000 000 / 1.12 = 5 357 143

2-yil: 8 000 000 / (1.12)^2 = 6 378 601

3-yil: 9 000 000 / (1.12)^3 = 6 406 069

4-yil: 10 000 000 / (1.12)^4 = 6 355 181

5-yil: 25 000 000 / (1.12)^5 = 14 186 566

Jami PV = 38 683 560 so'm

NPV = 38 683 560 - 30 000 000 = +8 683 560 so'm

Aksiya - kompaniyaga egalik huquqi. Uning qiymati = barcha kelajakdagi dividendlar va sotish narxining joriy qiymati. Amalda soddaroq ko'rsatkichlar ham ishlatiladi:

  • P/E nisbati (Narx/Daromad): Aksiya bahosi / Aksiya boshiga daromad. Kompaniya har

aksiyadan 5 000 so'm ishlab, bozordan P/E = 15 bo'lsa, aksiya qiymati = 75 000 so'm bo'lishi kerak. Past P/E - arzonlashgan, yuqori P/E - qimmatlashgan signal bo'lishi mumkin.

  • DCF (Diskontlangan pul oqimlari): Kompaniyaning kelajakdagi barcha erkin pul oqimlarini

prognoz qilish va ularni bugunga diskontlash. Bu professional analitiklar ishlatiladigan eng to'liq baholash usuli.

Ko'chmas mulkni baholash

Ko'chmas mulk baholash uchun ikkita asosiy yondashuv mavjud, ikkalasi ham diskontlangan pul oqimlari tamoyiliga asoslanadi:

  • Daromad yondashuvi: Qiymat = barcha kelajakdagi ijara daromadlarining PV + sotish

narxining PV. Bu NPV ni ko'chmas mulkka qo'llash.

  • Bozor yondashuvi: O'xshash mulklarning so'nggi sotish narqlari bilan taqqoslash. Bu oddiyroq,

lekin etarli bozor ma'lumotlari talab qiladi.

Oylik ijara (barcha xarajatlardan keyin sof): 2 500 000 so'm = 30 000 000 so'm/yil

10 yildan keyin kutilgan sotish narxi: 400 000 000 so'm

Siz talab qilgan daromad (alternativ xarajat): 10% yillik

10 yillik ijara oqimining PV (annuitet, 10%): taxminan 184 337 000 so'm

Sotish narxining PV: 400 000 000 / (1.10)^10 = 154 217 000 so'm

Jami ichki qiymat = 184 337 000 + 154 217 000 = 338 554 000 so'm

Ichki qiymat (338.6 mln) > So'ralayotgan narx (250 mln)

NPV = +88 554 000 so'm - bu narxda kvartira sotib olish foydali!

lessons.title: Risk va daromad
lessons.html:
Yuqori kutilgan daromad har doim yuqori risk bilan keladi. Bu moliyaning o'zgarmas qonuni. Kim risksiz yuqori daromad va'da qilsa - yo aldayapti, yo o'zi xato qilyapti.

Moliyada 'risk' nima?

Kundalik hayotda 'xavf' deganda yomon narsa sodir bo'lishi tushuniladi. Moliyada risk aniqroq: kelajakdagi daromadning noaniqligi va o'zgaruvchanligi.

Bank depoziti 14% kafolatlangan - past risk, aniq natija. Startup kompaniyasi 0% yoki 300% berishi mumkin - keng imkoniyatlar diapazoni, mana shu risk.

Risk turlari

  • Bozor riski (Tizimli risk): Barcha investitsiyalarga bir vaqtda ta'sir qiladigan xavf - iqtisodiy

inqiroz, urush, pandamiya. Diversifikatsiya bilan yo'q qilib bo'lmaydi.

Diversifikatsiya - investitsiyalarni turli aktivlar, sohalar va mintaqalarga taqsimlash, shu orqali kutilgan daromadni kamaytirmasdan risk darajasini tushirish. Bu moliyada yagona chinakam 'bepul tushlik'.

Pulning

Bugungi pul kelajakdagi bir xil summadan qimmatroq ekanligi tamoyili. Sabablari: investitsiya imkoniyati, inflyatsiya va noaniqlik riski.

Joriy qiymat (PV)

Kelajakdagi summaning bugungi qiymati - diskontlash orqali hisoblanadi. Formula: PV = FV / (1 + r)^n.

Kelajak

qiymati

(FV)

Bugungi summaning kelajakdagi qiymati - murakkab foiz bilan hisoblanadi. Formula: FV = PV x (1 + r)^n.

Diskontlash

Kelajakdagi pul oqimini joriy qiymatga aylantirish jarayoni. Vaqt qiymati va riskni hisobga oladi.

Diskont stavkasi

Kelajakdagi pul oqimlarini joriy qiymatga aylantirish uchun ishlatiladigan

foiz

Asosiy summa VA to'plangan foizlar ustidan foiz hisoblash. Boylikni eksponent tarzda o'stiradi. Moliyaning eng kuchli vositasi.

Oddiy foiz

Faqat boshlang'ich asosiy summa ustidan foiz hisoblash. Chiziqli o'sish - murakkab foizga qaraganda ancha kuchsiz.

Kelajak pul oqimlarining joriy qiymati minus boshlang'ich sarmoya. NPV > 0 = qiymat yaratadi, investitsiya qiling. NPV < 0 = rad eting.

Ichki qiymat

Aktivning asosiy tahlilga asoslangan haqiqiy iqtisodiy qiymati - barcha kutilgan kelajak pul oqimlarining joriy qiymati.

Baholash

Aktiv yoki biznesning haqiqiy qiymatini aniqlash jarayoni - odatda diskontlangan pul oqimlari tahlili orqali.

test.prompt: Bugungi pulning kelajakdagi bir xil summadan qimmatroq bo'lishining ASOSIY sabablarini eng to'g'ri ifodalovchi javob qaysi?
choices: Chunki bugungi pulni investitsiya qilish mumkin, inflyatsiya real qiymatni kamaytiradi va kelajak noaniq
Chunki hukumat odamlarni hozir sarflashga undaydi
Chunki banklar pul saqlash uchun komissiya oladi
test.explanation: Uchala sabab: investitsiya imkoniyati (daromad), inflyatsiya (sotib olish qobiliyati) va noaniqlik riski - hammasi birgalikda bugungi pulni qimmatroq qiladi.

test.prompt: PV = FV / (1+r)^n formulasini qo'llab: diskont stavkasi 10% bo'lganda 2 yildan keyin keladigan 8 000 000 so'mning joriy qiymati qancha?
Diskont stavkasi oshsa, kelajakdagi pul oqimining joriy qiymatiga nima bo'ladi?
test.explanation: Stavka oshsa - kelajakdagi pul oqimi kuchliroq diskontlanadi → joriy qiymati kamayadi.

test.prompt: 2 000 000 so'mni 5 yil davomida 10% murakkab foiz bilan investitsiya qilsangiz, taxminiy kelajak qiymati qancha?
72 qoidasiga ko'ra, 8% yillik murakkab foizda pul taxminan necha yilda ikki barobar bo'ladi?
test.explanation: 72 / 8 = 9 yil. 8% murakkab foizda pul taxminan har 9 yilda ikki barobar bo'ladi.

test.prompt: ZI ZI ZI ZI $ $ $ $ $ $ $ $ Sizda 15 000 000 so'm bor. Bank 13% taklif qilmoqda. Siz 20% kutilgan daromadli biznesni tanladingiz. Kapital alternativ xarajati qancha?
test.explanation: Alternativ xarajat = voz kechilgan eng yaxshi muqobil = 13% (bank). Biznes undan ko'proq ishlashi kerak, aks holda mantiqsiz.

test.prompt: Investitsiya yillik 11% daromad kutadi. Kapital alternativ xarajati 14%. Investitsiya qilish kerakmi?
choices: Yo'q - daromad alternativ xarajatdan past, NPV manfiy
test.explanation: 11% < 14% → NPV manfiy → investitsiya bankdan kamroq daromad beradi → rad eting.

test.prompt: Biznes 50 000 000 so'mga sotilmoqda. Barcha kelajak pul oqimlarining joriy qiymati = 62 000 000 so'm. NPV qancha va nima qilish kerak?
test.explanation: NPV = 62 000 000 - 50 000 000 = +12 000 000 so'm. Musbat NPV → sotib oling.

test.prompt: Markaziy bank foiz stavkalarini keskin oshirdi. Obligatsiyalar narxiga nima bo'ladi?
choices: Ko'tariladi - yuqori stavka ko'proq daromad beradi
Tushadi - belgilangan kelajak to'lovlar endi yuqori stavkada diskontlanadi
test.explanation: Stavka oshganda diskont stavkasi ko'payadi → belgilangan obligatsiya to'lovlarining joriy qiymati tushadi → obligatsiya narxi pasayadi.

test.prompt: Quyidagi aktivlarning to'g'ri risk tartibini (pasidan balandiga) ko'rsating:
choices: Startup → Ko'chmas mulk → Bank depoziti → Davlat obligatsiyasi
Bank depoziti → Davlat obligatsiyasi → Ko'chmas mulk → Startup
Davlat obligatsiyasi → Startup → Bank depoziti → Ko'chmas mulk
Ko'chmas mulk → Bank depoziti → Startup → Davlat obligatsiyasi
test.explanation: To'g'ri tartib: Bank depoziti (eng xavfsiz) → Davlat obligatsiyasi → Ko'chmas mulk → Startup (eng xavfli).

test.prompt: Investor barcha pulini bitta kompaniya aksiyasiga qo'ydi. Konsultant 50 ta kompaniya, 10 ta soha va 5 ta mamlakat bo'ylab taqsimlashni maslahat berdi. Bu qaysi tamoyil?
test.explanation: Sohalar va mamlakatlar bo'ylab tarqatish - klassik diversifikatsiya. Kutilgan daromad kamaymaydi, lekin spetsifik risk kamayadi.

test.prompt: Quyidagi fikrlardan qaysi biri NOTO'G'RI? ZI ZI ZI ZI $ $ $ $ $ $ $ $
choices: Inflyatsiya pulning sotib olish qobiliyatini kamaytiradi
Harakatsizlik bepul tanlov - pul shunchaki saqlanadi
Har qanday summaning vaqt qiymati bor
Yuqori daromad har doim yuqori risk bilan keladi ZI ZI ZI ZI $ $ $ $ $ $ $ $ Javoblar va tushuntirishlar
test.explanation: NOTO'G'RI fikr: harakatsizlik bepul emas - inflyatsiya va alternativ xarajat tufayli har yili real qiymat yo'qoladi. Natija bo'yicha yo'riqnoma 12/12: Ajoyib - 2-Blok to'liq o'zlashtirildi. 3-Blokka o'tishga tayyor! 10-11: Juda yaxshi - o'tkazib yuborilgan savollarni qayta ko'ring. 8-9: Yaxshi - 2.3 va 2.5 bo'limlarni misollar bilan qayta o'qing. 6-7: Qoniqarli - barcha 6 bo'limni lug'at bilan birgalikda takrorlang. 6 dan past: Boshidan qayta o'qing, formulalar va misollarga alohida e'tibor bering.
